title: Stupid & Evil Business Model - Buy Now Pay Later
summary: Comedic deep-dive video arguing BNPL functions like an unregulated, more dangerous version of a credit card.

assertions.quote: they charge 3 to 6%, aka double what a credit card charges
CLA isn't giving you access to a line of credit. They're giving you an individual loan
you've got 30 loans out there auto withdrawing from your account on whatever random dates
they don't run your credit. So... it's never going to improve your credit score
if retail companies are going to have to pay an extra 3%, they're going to pass that along to the customer

verdicts.note: Merchant fees for BNPL are well documented as higher than card processing fees, but the price-wide pass-through claim has less direct evidence.
NBER: the merchant cost of providing BNPL in this dataset was about 2.1% of BNPL-financed revenue, close to Klarna's reported 2.02% and Affirm's reported 2.51% of gross merchandise value.

assertions.quote: they're 20% more likely to make the purchase and they're 30% more likely to spend even more money
they don't do that same screening process at all... giving individual loans... to people that probably can't afford to pay it back

verdicts.note: CFPB: 'because most BNPL lenders only make "soft" credit bureau inquiries,' approval doesn't require the hard pull and income verification a traditional lender's underwriting process would involve.
